playbook:
**Playbook for sonar picket games:**

**Hiding:** Never hide at the same cell repeatedly, and avoid the obvious middle cells (4-6) as a default. Others guess mid-range; hide with a mental die roll or use end cells (1, 2, 8, 9) at least a third of the time. This worked again — Gamma fired at me round after round per the standing order and never hit me while I moved cells. Keep changing cells every round unless there's a specific reason to stay.

**Firing:** The standing order fixes my *target*, so the only freedom is the cell. My picks this run were scattered and mostly wrong — 1 hit in 6 shots. Two fixes: (1) re-read the relayed hit/miss log each round *before* choosing a cell — if the target has taken a hit recently, they were in a concrete cell and may return to it or move one step; prefer that neighborhood over pure random. (2) Don't fire at my own hidden cell's neighbors out of habit — my guesses clustered where I myself was thinking, which is not where Foxtrot was. Vary cells, but vary them *informed*, not evenly.

**Harbor:** Do not fire on Harbor. The payoff is only 3 points and the standing threat is removal from the board, forfeiting all future scoring. Never worth it. Held up again — Harbor never fired and never hurt me.

**Claims:** Always claim the true result. The office enforces truth; honesty costs nothing. Keep exactly as is.

**Escort claims — verify the boat name before naming it.** I wrote "[salvage: Delta]" again in the final round when the board was Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor. This is a recurring failure and it costs me a live lottery ticket every time. Hard rule: before typing the salvage token, read the boat names off the current points table and pick one of those, verbatim. Wrong names score nothing; a valid name at least has a chance to pay 5 if it names me back. Nobody has ever matched my escort offers, so don't *plan* on escort income — it's a bonus, not part of the engine.

**Notes:** Use them for dealmaking, short and actionable. But expect no takers: in two full runs my mutual-escort offers have never been accepted, and opponents default to filler like "steady on station." Post a one-line standing offer in round 1, repeat it briefly once mid-game and once in the final round, and spend no more attention on it. The notes channel is worth almost nothing in practice.

**Endgame:** Final round with the score known: take the highest-EV action. The core engine is hits (4 each) plus not getting hit — my entire +4 came from one round-1 hit. Don't sacrifice a good shot choice for dealmaking that won't stick. Do spend the last round's fire decision carefully: one more informed cell choice is worth more than any note.

**Overall:** The reliable engine is unchanged: hide unpredictably at varied cells (ends favored), comply with standing orders for targets but choose fire cells from the target's observed pattern rather than uniformly at random, claim truthfully, never touch Harbor. The recurring losses are self-inflicted: invalid escort names (fix by reading the points table first) and uninformed fire cells (fix by reading the shot log before firing). Fix those two habits and the score is hits × 4 minus hits taken.

PLAYBOOK

Claims: when the office tells me my true result, I claim exactly that. The rules say the public claim must match the private result; lying gains nothing and risks penalty or lost credibility. This worked cleanly every round — keep it.

Escorts: the mutual escort payoff is 5 points each, the biggest single payoff, and I never collected it — again. Explicit notes offering an escort got no takers over two full games, and switching partners mid-game didn't help either. Keep trying cheaply: name a boat every round (never "none" — an unmatched claim costs nothing), put one clear escort offer in a note ("Foxtrot offers escort to X — name me back"), and switch the named boat if two rounds pass with no payout. But don't sink effort or risk into coordination that keeps failing — treat escort points as a bonus, not the plan. The note offer costs nothing if refused, so keep making it, but don't let it shape anything else I do.

Hiding: avoid the center cell — it's the default shot. Wings held up again: my shooter missed me most rounds while I varied wing cells. Vary cells between rounds so a pattern-reader can't track me, but don't revisit recently-fired cells. This is settled; keep it.

Firing: wing cells are the money. I hit Gamma repeatedly at cell 8 and again at cell 2 in the final round — varied wing shots produced multiple 4-point hits and drove my score to +15. Follow the standing order target each round, spread shots across wing cells rather than center, and keep varying: repeated identical cells miss, fresh wing cells hit. Keep the one center-ish probe early if unused cells are scarce, but wings first.

Standing order vs. Harbor: don't fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting but the standing signal says I'm put off the board for the rest of the patrol — game over. Not worth it unless I'm already far behind late with nothing to lose.

Notes: keep them bland except when carrying one escort offer. Revealing anything about my position or plans is free information for the boat shooting at me. Note stage comes after hiding but before firing — timing means my note can't reveal where I just hid, but it can leak my intentions, so keep it minimal.

Overall priority: reliable scoring comes from honest claiming plus varied wing firing at the standing-order target — that alone produced a strong positive score with zero escort points. Pursue the escort pair cheaply (name someone every round, one clear note offer, switch partners when stale), but budget no further effort for it. Avoid center when hiding, never fire the same cell twice in a row, and never touch Harbor.

# Playbook — Sonar Picket (as a shooting boat)

**Hiding.** Off-center alone is not enough — this game Foxtrot hit me three times while I varied among off-center cells. Opponents do track my pattern and bracket me. Do more than "avoid 5": randomize genuinely across {1,2,3,7,8,9}, and avoid repeating a cell or side I was just hit on. If a specific boat has hit me twice, treat my previous cells as burned and jump to the far end plus one. But accept some hits are unavoidable; don't burn mental effort over-optimizing.

**Notes.** "Steady on station" is the local convention — Echo and Foxtrot posted it every round and ignored my escort proposal completely. Proposing once early is still worth one round's note, but if the reply is another "steady on station," drop it and stop asking. Don't spend multiple rounds negotiating with a wall.

**Firing.** Keep the standing-order discipline and the never-fire-at-Harbor rule — that part held up. The escalation ladder (5 first, then 4/6, then off-center) is right in principle but I executed it too predictably: after two misses at a target I was still shooting adjacent cells (4 twice at Echo). Once I've missed twice at the same target, jump far — 2 or 8 — not one step over. If the target keeps missing me from the same neighborhood, remember they're likely moving too; consider the cells adjacent to where they last dodged rather than where I last shot.

**Claims.** Always truthful — the office forces it. No decision here.

**Escort claims.** Critical correction: an unreciprocated claim pays ZERO, not "something rather than nothing." This game I claimed escorts anyway on the theory it beat "none" — it didn't, and I even claimed a boat that doesn't exist (Delta — there are only Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor; check the roster). Claim a boat ONLY if their note or prior claim shows real reciprocation. If both partners stonewall all game (as they did here), salvage: none is correct every round and costs nothing. The 5+5 payoff requires actual mutual engagement; unilaterally claiming never manufactures it.

**Scoring math to remember.** Hits pay 4 to me and cost the target 1; being hit costs me only 1 per hit, so the hit race matters more than the damage race — keep hunting my own hits rather than playing pure defense. But this game the reliable payoffs never materialized (no hits, no escorts) and I finished -4 from being hit. Lesson: when escort coordination fails by round 2, all my points must come from landing hits — so put real effort into reading the opponent's hiding pattern instead of drifting through formula shots.

**What didn't work:** firing 5 then adjacent cells at the same target for six rounds — zero hits. Waiting for note-based coordination that never came, then claiming escorts anyway (including a nonexistent boat) — zero points. Varying hide cells within one side of the map — Foxtrot still found me repeatedly. **What worked / keep:** truthful claims, never firing at Harbor, following the standing order, proposing escort exactly once early.
